newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to launch rand/dollar futures April 30.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to launch rand/dollar futures April 30.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange (Safex) said on Tuesday that it would start trading a rand/dollar futures contract and options thereon from April 30.
The exchange said in a statement that the authorities had approved the futures and options contracts on Monday.

Approval in principle for the futures contract was given in the March 12 budget, as part of the ongoing relaxation of exchange controls. Trade in the contracts will initially be limited to non-resident clients of Safex members and authorised dealers.

Residents with an exposure to the rand/dollar exchange rate will be able to hedge by obtaining a forward deal through authorised dealers. They in turn will be able to offset the risk either in the forward cover market or via futures.
Safex members will be able to trade, as agent, with non-resident clients and authorised dealers.

The Reserve Bank agreed that trading in rand futures should evolve in line with the broader process of relaxing exchange controls and the restrictions will be gradually lifted until the products are freely traded locally and abroad, Safex said.
The underlying instrument on the futures will be the spot rand/dollar exchange rate, quoted to four decimal places, and contracts will be valued at $100,000 each.

Expiry dates would follow the same cycle as equity contracts -- March, June, September and December -- with expiry prices determined by taking a notional offer to buy and sell from six authorised dealers at the expiry time, followed by the arithmetic average of the middle four rates.
The futures will be cash settled in rand.
Safex will list options on futures with strike prices at intervals of 0.01 rand/dollar.
